title: Object.assign and Merging Check
description: Shallow merge with Object.assign and object spread.

questions.explanation: Target `{}` receives copies. Later `prefs` overwrites `lang`. `defaults` is not the target, so it stays intact.

questions.prompt: What is the modern literal equivalent of `Object.assign({}, a, b)`?
questions.explanation: Object spread performs the same shallow merge into a new object.

options.text: Mutates `target` by copying properties onto it
Always returns a brand-new object and leaves `target` alone

questions.explanation: The first argument is the mutable target. Pass `{}` when you want a new object.

questions.prompt: Is `Object.assign` / `{ ... }` a deep merge for nested objects?

options.text: No — nested objects are replaced wholesale (shallow)
Yes — nested keys are merged recursively
Only when both sides have the same keys

questions.explanation: `{ nested: { a: 1 } }` merged with `{ nested: { b: 2 } }` yields `{ nested: { b: 2 } }`, not `{ a: 1, b: 2 }`.

questions.prompt: In `Object.assign({}, { x: 1 }, { x: 2 }, { x: 3 })`, what is `x`?
questions.explanation: Sources are applied left to right; the last write to `x` remains.
